puzzle.instruction: Apply both changes from the worked pair.
puzzle.explanation: The worked pair shows two clear changes. The whole board rotates 2 quarter-turns clockwise, while every token advances 2 steps through outline, half, and solid fill. puzzle.instruction: Apply the same spatial transformation.

Every distractor is the output of another bounded rotation, reflection, or wrapped shift that fails the worked pair.

puzzle.instruction: The first pair undoes two changes. Which scene similarly precedes the third?
puzzle.explanation: The first pair is shown in reverse order: the second board becomes the first after the board rotates 1 quarter-turn clockwise and every fill advances 2 steps. Test each option as the missing input and apply both changes. Only the highlighted input produces the third board exactly. Each distractor would work under another bounded spatial-and-fill program, but that program fails the worked pair.

puzzle.instruction: Use the fold arrow and worked pair. Which folded punch produces the third board?
puzzle.explanation: Work backward from the open query board using the worked crease program: vertical:leftToRight. Mirrored punches overlap when each indicated side folds across its centre line, leaving the single punch shown by the highlighted folded board. Its punch position, crease axes, and arrows all match the worked pair. The other options use a different bounded fold program, so they either unfold to another pattern or contradict the demonstrated directions.

puzzle.instruction: Each gate has a demonstrated rule. Apply only the gate shown in the query path.

puzzle.instruction: Infer the row operation and the column operation. Which board satisfies both?

Down each column, the bottom board keeps every occupied position from either input. Applying both rules to the missing corner produces the same highlighted board; every distractor comes from a set rule that fails a worked row or column, from the right rule applied to the two boards in the wrong order, or from copying one of those two boards instead of combining them.

The highlighted completion preserves every shown cell and supplies that value. Each distractor changes only the missing tile but breaks at least one visible equality or difference in the grouping.
